text:
Jordan (Sales): Hey team — OrbitHealth POC demo tomorrow 10:00am PT. They expect ~70-90 concurrent requests for a 15-minute live demo. Request: temporary capacity bump or burst policy so they don't hit throttles. Who can provision and what's the fastest path? Also need ballpark cost for approval.

Priya (SE): Quick q — what's the average tokens per request and model they're using? That drives vCPU/GPU load. If it's static prompts we can use smaller quantized variant.

Jordan (Sales): They're testing chat completions using our recommended open/llama-13b-quant variant, ~800 tokens avg per response. Demo traffic concentrated to a 10–15m window.

Priya (SE): OK. Two practical options: 1) Temporary Dedicated pool reservation for the window (most predictable latency, but needs lead time and commit), or 2) Enable burst credits on their existing dedicated pool (fast, no long-term commit) — we can top up N tokens of burst quota for demo. For 70–90 concurrent @ ~800 tokens I'd estimate ~5M tokens for 15m (including overhead). Suggest burst_quota=6_000_000 to be safe.

Ethan (Infra): FYI operational constraints: full reserved capacity (new GPUs) normally 24–48h to spin up if capacity not immediately free. If existing pool has slack we can reassign capacity instantly. Burst credits we can enable same day. If we need new physical nodes and after-hours provisioning, expect 4–6h at best with on-call.

Alex (ProdOps): I can create a temporary pool and attach a burst policy now. Proposed config below — can be applied immediately and set to auto-teardown after 72h: ```yaml
pool_name: poc-orbit-demo
model: open/llama-13b-quant
min_replicas: 2
max_replicas: 12
burst_enabled: true
burst_quota: 6000000
burst_window: 30m
auto_teardown: 72h
```
CLI to create quickly: `rwctl dedicated create --name poc-orbit-demo --model open/llama-13b-quant --min 2 --max 12 --burst-quota 6000000 --burst-window 30m --ttl 72h`

Priya (SE): That looks good. Also enable prefix KV caching for the demo routes to reduce token regen. I can add a routing rule to prioritize demo traffic to this pool: `route: demo.orbithealth.com -> poc-orbit-demo`

Jordan (Sales): Thanks — what's the estimated cost for the 72h pool with that max_replicas=12 config vs burst only? Need a number for procurement.

Ethan (Infra): Ballpark: burst-only (6M tokens) ~ $2.4k in token-equivalent billing (estimate depends on model). Temporary pool with max=12 GPUs for 3 days — if fully utilized could be ~ $18k-$25k depending on GPU type. If we assume they won't hit sustained max, expected cost likely $3k-$8k. I'll add fine-grain estimate when I know expected sustained RPS.

Jordan (Sales): I'll get customer to cap RPS if needed. For speed, go ahead with burst_quota=6_000_000 and the routing rule. Proceed once I confirm procurement sign-off. :thumbsup:

Alex (ProdOps): Will provision burst and create the pool in dry-run mode (no billing commit) so you can demo. If procurement approves, we flip billing and keep pool live. Creating dry-run now.

deploy-bot: created dedicated pool "poc-orbit-demo" in dry-run mode (id: dp-7f4c). Autoscale policy applied.

Priya (SE): I pushed the route to point demo traffic to the pool and enabled KV prefix caching for `/demo/*`. Please test from the staging link.

Jordan (Sales): Verified from my side — demo traffic flows to poc-orbit-demo, latency looks stable at p95 ~220ms. Sending cost approval email now.

Ethan (Infra): Once procurement confirms, reply here and I'll convert dry-run to billed reservation and lock the burst_quota. If procurement denies, we can keep burst-only for demo window and teardown automatically.

Jordan (Sales): Procurement approved. Convert to billed reservation and enable the full burst quota for tomorrow 09:30–11:00 PT.

Alex (ProdOps): On it. Converting now. You'll get a billing confirmation shortly. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: billing change completed for dp-7f4c — reservation active, burst_quota=6000000, ttl=72h.

Jordan (Sales): Amazing — thanks everyone. Will run the demo and update thread after.

Priya (SE): Good luck — ping if any throttles show up and we can temporarily scale further.

Ethan (Infra): Monitoring alerts added for cpu/gpu saturation and queue depth. I'll be on standby.
